degreeAudit.universalInduction: The displayed inequalities hold for every j>=1 and 1<=k<=j. Finite rows are regression checks of these same affine identities, not extrapolation of observed derivative values.

proof.domain: Fixed selected band ell=ellMinimum+8; frozen representative with Xplus<Xrep<=Xb, etaRep in[-1,1], sRep in[1/2,2]. Observe X=Xb*exp(-delta), 0<=delta<=1/2, eta in[-1,1], s in[1/2,2], in the same source box with slow distance<=4/S^3. Apply the zero-extension statement near its intersection with X=Xb.
proof.chartBoundary: Smoothness in the open eta chart; at eta=+/-1 all mixed jets are the original one-sided heat boundary jets. No continuation of the real heat integral to negative T is asserted.
proof.sourceEquality: Every positive-order completed field has the same zero exterior X>Xplus. This includes a neighborhood on both sides of Xb. Thus the actual complete background, not a truncated active prefix, equals the retained leading field there.
proof.exactFactor: On this collar heatCutoff=1 and U=0. Original A.8 uses regular-axis/full-moment identities to replace the forward target by its exact backward representation A.53/A.54. Substitute u=delta/sqrt(1+delta^2*t) in each f_o_prime integral. All three angular terms, the full heat pressure square and both axial integrations remain. This is an analytic integral identity, not a rational simplification of the retained forward target.
proof.endpoint: The regularized Laplace integrals have endpoint G(0)/4 and every finite mixed derivative is dominated by exp(-4t) times a polynomial in t. The explicit coefficient b_theta(0)=16*rho*EpowB*H(2d/Xb)*exp(1)/sqrt(2Xb)>0. The scaled axial coefficient is delta^6*b_z and hence zero at0.
proof.coefficientPositivity: Use the limiting direction of (b_theta,delta^6*b_z), not the zero stress vector. Its source lower b_theta>=C^-10 and frozen projection -N dot n>Renv^-33 imply tauTilde>Renv^-56. The actual normalized covariance cone and positive masses give W_i>=kappa*tauTilde/(64*massUpper)>0, including delta=0 by continuity. At a boundary representative the same source closed-annulus primitive bounds and rounding error apply directly; continuity of discrete labels is never assumed.
proof.smoothInverse: On the closed one-sided outer chart all fixed finite leading jets are bounded: the terminal formula is a product of elementary smooth factors, the actual square-seed step, and the full Laplace heat with |H^(j)(z)|<=(h)_j*(1+h)_j for z>=0. The pulse coefficients have the original protected denominators, a finite interval and frozen labels. Parameter differentiation of the explicit Volterra series is justified by its finite-order augmented factorial majorant. H and its nonvanishing inverse, bbar and positive W are therefore smooth up to this radial edge.
proof.stablePulse: The executed matrix identity retains the reference diagonal (0,-2lambda). Its induced logarithmic norm is at most(2E+Ed)/S; the resulting forward propagator bound is independent of S. Taking an absolute matrix norm would discard this useful negative diagonal and is not the argument used here.
proof.finiteSourceJetConstants: For each fixed order j, the leading outer field and chart jets on the fixed compact profile collar have finite source-only bounds. Frozen c0,lambda0,Bs,carrier p,pz and their reciprocals that actually occur have the source bounds; epsilon*k^2 is in[1,4]. No bare k occurs in M except through this product and bounded frozen carriers. Every j>=1 slow jet of n is O(S), while n_prime jets are O(1); the source tangent/normal denominators have positive source-only lower bounds. The finite product/chain rules give M_j,B_j=O(S^j). This argument concerns ordinary slow derivatives, with all labels fixed.
proof.pulseJetRecurrence: w_alpha_prime=M*w_alpha+sum_(0<beta<=alpha) binom(alpha,beta) M_beta*w_(alpha-beta), with zero derivative initial data. Variation of constants and Ls<=Lmax*S give w_j=O(S^(2j)). P has exactly zero slow-point derivatives, hence t_j/P=O(S^(2j)). The same argument bounds mixed profile derivatives after the fixed smooth chart conversion.
proof.determinantScale: The exact lower expression equals (15/16)*Ac*u*Dg^2*r0*(Integral chi^2)^2*massLowerCoefficient^2*ci. The source inequalities Ac>Renv^-6 and ci>1/(Tg*S) give the returned strictly positive source-only determinantScaledLower/S. The source cone yields |t_tan|<=8*u*Renv^10*t_r, so each |H_ij|<=covarianceEntryUpper. The 2x2 adjugate therefore gives ||H^-1||_infinity<=inverseScaleUpper*S. These constants are actual expression roots, not an unspecified determinant premise.
proof.inverseJetRecurrence: The exact cancellation haar*Ls=Dg*r0*Integral chi^2 gives H_j=O(S^(2j)). The separate determinant-scale identity and positive source-only lower give ||H^-1||=O(S). Differentiating H*W=bbar inductively gives W_j=O(S^(3j+1)). The positive W lower uses massUpper, which is independent of S. The sqrt recurrence then gives (sqrt W)_j=O(S^(4j)) for j>=1, and its value is O(S). Every constant is finite and depends only on the fixed source and derivative order; the individual numerical constants have not been evaluated by this certificate.
proof.flatZeroExtension: sqrt(y_i)=exp(-2/delta^2)*delta^(-3/2)*sqrt(W_i) for delta>0. The exact scalar recurrence gives every derivative an arbitrary extra power delta^N. Leibniz and the preceding bounds yield |D^I sqrt(y_i)|<=C_(I,N)*S^(4|I|+1)*delta^N. At delta<=0 define the whole function as0, before evaluating an interior square root. All jets match0 at the edge. The raw actual forward target remains in the graph; its zero exterior follows the original backward/full-moment identity.
proof.uniformity: The polynomial-in-S estimates are a written source-bound derivative theorem with explicit degree recurrences and existing actual primitive bounds. They are not a numerical enclosure of H, an execution of every derivative order, or a new Lean kernel theorem.
